title: A student-loan servicing order specifies redress reachability and later institutional completion without exposing borrower-level recovery
source_unit: CFPB Wells Fargo private student-loan servicing consent order and order-termination record
geography: United States borrowers affected by Wells Fargo private student-loan servicing

denominator.unit: affected borrowers under the consent order; the retained public record does not expose the final person-level list

redress_reachability_requirement.value: identify affected consumers, calculate individual amounts, issue payments, attempt to locate recipients, and follow up on returned or uncashed payments

correction_scope.value: servicing, disclosures, fees, payment consequences, and inaccurate credit-reporting practices were subject to corrective requirements

borrower_receipt.unit: missing person-level payment date, delivery, cashing, account correction, adequacy, residual loss, trust, and exit

observations.method: Extraction from the official CFPB consent order; redress-plan identification, payment, returned-payment follow-up, and credit-reporting correction requirements are kept separate from borrower-level completion.
observations.uncertainty: The order defines an institutional process but does not provide the final affected-borrower list or individual payment and account records in this retained layer. The $410,000 floor is not a per-borrower amount or recovery rate.
observations.subgroup: Borrowers affected by the servicing, fee, payment-consequence, disclosure, or credit-reporting practices addressed by the order; demographic and financial-vulnerability subgroup outcomes are not public here.
observations.counterinterpretation: A detailed follow-up obligation can improve reachability while still failing to reveal which borrowers were paid, reached, or made whole; formal design is not lived recovery.

denominator.unit: consent-order obligations; borrower-level completion denominator is not published in the retained record

institutional_completion.value: CFPB reported that Wells Fargo fulfilled its obligations and terminated the order

reported_completion_components.value: remediation to specified consumers, reasonable furnishing policies, and redress of inaccurate furnishing for impacted consumers

borrower_level_recovery.unit: formal termination does not expose payment receipt, account state, credit correction, adequacy, residual loss, later borrowing, trust, or switching

observations.method: Extraction from the official CFPB termination document; formal closure is retained as an institutional endpoint and not converted into universal borrower receipt or recovery.
observations.uncertainty: The termination record is an agency-reported completion statement. It does not provide the person-level list, payment and correction timing, failed or returned payment count, adequacy, or later household and financial outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Borrowers covered by the original order and reported remediation; no borrower-level subgroup or later use outcome is available.
observations.counterinterpretation: The agency's completion statement may correspond to adequate remedy for affected borrowers, but the public record retained here cannot test that counterexample at the borrower level.

related_sources.claim: The CFPB case materials provide the enforcement context for Wells Fargo student-loan servicing and redress.
The CFPB student-loan consumer-protection context provides the relevant borrower-service domain.

boundary: This record follows a named student-loan servicing route from alleged fees, payment confusion, and credit-reporting problems through an ordered redress/reachability design and later institutional termination. It does not establish borrower-level delivery, account correction, adequacy, household recovery, trust, continued borrowing, switching, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official CFPB consent-order and order-termination PDFs were directly retrieved and hashed on 2026-10-20.
